# Shell-style quoting for GRAPH_EXECUTION_*_ARGS

## What to build

Jira KAN-72 / GE-11. Every real provider appends extra CLI flags from an env var — `GRAPH_EXECUTION_CLAUDE_ARGS`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_CODEX_ARGS`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_OPENCODE_ARGS`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_QWEN_ARGS` — but each one does `env[X_ARGS_ENV]?.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)`, so quoting is ignored: `--append-system-prompt "two words"` becomes the three argv entries `--append-system-prompt`, `"two`, `words"`. Add ONE shared helper, `splitArgs`, in a new file `src/providers/args.ts` that splits a string with small POSIX-shell-style rules (no new npm dependency), use it in all 4 providers, make a malformed value (unterminated quote) fail at startup with a clear message, and document the quoting in the README. The args are passed to the CLI as an argv array (`spawnAgent(bin, args, …)`, no shell), so the helper only tokenises; it never expands variables, globs or `~`.

Expected results:
- `"two words"` → `["two words"]`, `'two words'` → `["two words"]`, `a\ b` → `["a b"]`
- `" --max-turns  5 "` → `["--max-turns", "5"]` (current behaviour for unquoted input is kept)
- `--x="a b"c` → `["--x=a bc"]` (adjacent quoted/unquoted pieces join into one word)
- `""` and `''` → `[""]` (an explicit empty argument); empty / whitespace-only / unset → `[]`
- `'it''s'` → `["its"]`; `"say \"hi\""` → `['say "hi"']`; `'a\b'` → `["a\\b"]` (backslash is literal in single quotes)
- `"unterminated`, `'x`, or a trailing lone `\` → throws `Error("GRAPH_EXECUTION_CLAUDE_ARGS: unterminated double quote")` (message names the env var and the problem)

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `src/providers/claude.ts` (lines 1–33) — header comment says "space-split" (line 7); `CLAUDE_ARGS_ENV` (line 25, doc comment line 24 "space-separated"); `claudeArgs` (lines 28–33) with the split at line 31.
- `src/providers/codex.ts` (lines 13–23) — `CODEX_ARGS_ENV` line 16, `codexArgs` split at line 21 (the `"-"` prompt marker must stay LAST).
- `src/providers/opencode.ts` (lines 13–23) — `OPENCODE_ARGS_ENV` line 16, split at line 21.
- `src/providers/qwen.ts` (lines 13–23) — `QWEN_ARGS_ENV` line 16, split at line 21.
- `src/providers/index.ts` (lines 40–65) — `getProvider(name, cwd)`: the startup check (`requireOnPath`) where a malformed env var should also fail fast.
- `src/providers/claude.test.ts` (lines 1–60, 97–102, 139–152) — fake `claude` binary that records argv to JSON; test "passes --model and appends extra args from the env". Same structure in `codex.test.ts` (101–107), `opencode.test.ts` (101–107), `qwen.test.ts` (101–107).
- `src/providers/tools.test.ts` (lines 1–30) — style for a pure-function unit test file in this folder.
- `README.md` line 16 (Requirements) — the only place the env vars are documented today (mentions `GRAPH_EXECUTION_QWEN_ARGS`).

## Patterns to follow

**Current code (identical in all 4 providers):**
```typescript
/** Extra CLI flags appended to every invocation, space-separated. */
export const CLAUDE_ARGS_ENV = "GRAPH_EXECUTION_CLAUDE_ARGS";

export function claudeArgs(opts: Pick<AgentRunOptions, "model">, env = process.env): string[] {
  const args = ["-p", "--dangerously-skip-permissions", "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose"];
  if (opts.model) args.push("--model", opts.model);
  const extra = env[CLAUDE_ARGS_ENV]?.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean) ?? [];
  return [...args, ...extra];
}
```
**Target:**
```typescript
import { splitArgs } from "./args.js";
...
  const extra = splitArgs(env[CLAUDE_ARGS_ENV], CLAUDE_ARGS_ENV);
```

**Naming / file conventions:** ESM with explicit `.js` import suffixes (`import { spawnAgent } from "./spawn.js";`); each module opens with a `/** … */` doc comment explaining what it does (see `src/providers/tools.ts:1–9`); named exports only; tests sit next to the file as `<name>.test.ts`.

**Error handling:** plain `Error` with a user-facing message, as in `src/providers/index.ts:42`:
```typescript
throw new Error(`the "${bin}" CLI was not found on the PATH; install it and log in before running`);
```

**Test pattern (pure function):**
```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { codexToolCalls, opencodeToolCalls, streamJsonToolCalls } from "./tools.js";
describe("streamJsonToolCalls (Claude Code, Qwen Code)", () => {
  it("returns the tool_use blocks of an assistant message", () => {
    expect(streamJsonToolCalls(claudeBash)).toEqual([...]);
  });
});
```
**Test pattern (provider argv, `src/providers/claude.test.ts:97–102`):**
```typescript
it("passes --model and appends extra args from the env", async () => {
  process.env[CLAUDE_ARGS_ENV] = " --max-turns  5 ";
  const run = claudeProvider.run(opts({ model: "opus" }));
  await run.done;
  expect((await recorded()).argv.slice(-4)).toEqual(["--model", "opus", "--max-turns", "5"]);
});
```
The `beforeEach` already saves/restores `CLAUDE_ARGS_ENV` (it is in `ENV_KEYS`), so new tests can set it freely.

## Step-by-step tasks

### CREATE `src/providers/args.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `export function splitArgs(value: string | undefined, name: string): string[]`. A single left-to-right character scan with a state of `none | single | double`, a `current` string and a `inWord` boolean (so `""` yields an empty argument):
  - state `none`: whitespace (`/\s/`) ends the current word if `inWord` (push it, reset); `'` → state `single`, `inWord = true`; `"` → state `double`, `inWord = true`; `\` → the next character is taken literally (`inWord = true`); if there is no next character, throw `trailing backslash`; any other char is appended (`inWord = true`).
  - state `single`: everything up to the next `'` is literal (backslash included); `'` → back to `none`.
  - state `double`: `"` → back to `none`; `\` followed by `"`, `\`, `$` or `` ` `` → append that next char; `\` followed by anything else → append the backslash itself (then the char is processed normally); other chars are appended.
  - at the end: state `single` → throw `unterminated single quote`; state `double` → throw `unterminated double quote`; if `inWord`, push `current`.
  - `undefined` / `""` / whitespace-only → `[]`.
  - errors: `throw new Error(`${name}: ${problem}`)`, e.g. `GRAPH_EXECUTION_CODEX_ARGS: unterminated single quote`.
  - Start the file with a doc comment saying: it splits a `GRAPH_EXECUTION_<NAME>_ARGS` value into argv words with POSIX-shell-style quoting (whitespace separates; single quotes are fully literal; double quotes allow backslash-escaping of the four characters double-quote, backslash, dollar and backtick; outside quotes a backslash escapes the next character), and that nothing is ever expanded because the words go to the CLI as argv, never through a shell.
- **PATTERN**: `src/providers/tools.ts` (small pure module with a header comment).
- **IMPORTS**: none.
- **GOTCHA**: do NOT add a dependency such as `shell-quote`/`string-argv` (package.json must not change). `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is on: `value[i]` is `string | undefined`; iterate with `for (let i = 0; i < value.length; i++) { const c = value[i]!; … }` or `Array.from(value)`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit`

### CREATE `src/providers/args.test.ts` (regression test)

- **IMPLEMENT**: `describe("splitArgs", …)` with one `it` per rule, using `expect(splitArgs(input, "X_ARGS")).toEqual([...])` for every example in "What to build" (the 3 ticket cases `"two words"`, `'two words'`, `a\ b` in one `it("keeps quoted and escaped words together (GE-11)")`), plus `undefined`, `""`, `"   "` → `[]`, tabs/newlines as separators, and `expect(() => splitArgs('"x', "X_ARGS")).toThrow("X_ARGS: unterminated double quote")`, same for `'x` (single) and `a\` (trailing backslash).
- **PATTERN**: `src/providers/tools.test.ts`.
- **IMPORTS**: `import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"; import { splitArgs } from "./args.js";`
- **GOTCHA**: write the inputs in TS carefully: `a\ b` is the TS literal `"a\\ b"`; `'a\b'` is `"'a\\b'"` and expects `["a\\b"]`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/providers/args.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/providers/claude.ts`, `src/providers/codex.ts`, `src/providers/opencode.ts`, `src/providers/qwen.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in each, add `import { splitArgs } from "./args.js";` (next to the `./spawn.js` import) and replace `env[X_ARGS_ENV]?.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean) ?? []` with `splitArgs(env[X_ARGS_ENV], X_ARGS_ENV)`. Change the doc comment above each `*_ARGS_ENV` from "space-separated" to "split with shell-style quoting (see `splitArgs`)". In `claude.ts` line 7 change "space-split" to "split with shell-style quoting by `splitArgs`".
- **PATTERN**: the target snippet above.
- **GOTCHA**: `codexArgs` must still return `[...args, ...extra, "-"]` (the `-` prompt marker last). Keep the `env = process.env` parameter so tests can pass an env.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/providers`

### UPDATE `src/providers/index.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `getProvider`, after each `await requireOnPath(...)` for claude/codex/opencode/qwen, build the args once so a malformed env var aborts the run at startup instead of failing every attempt: e.g. `claudeArgs({});` (import `claudeArgs`, `codexArgs`, `opencodeArgs`, `qwenArgs` from their modules). It throws the `splitArgs` error, which the caller already reports like the missing-CLI error.
- **PATTERN**: `requireOnPath` in the same file (startup check, PRD §7.11).
- **GOTCHA**: do not do this for the `fake` provider. The `opts` type is `Pick<AgentRunOptions, "model">`; `{}` is valid since `model` is optional.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/providers/claude.test.ts src/providers/index.test.ts`

### UPDATE provider tests `src/providers/claude.test.ts`, `codex.test.ts`, `opencode.test.ts`, `qwen.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in each, add a test right after "passes --model and appends extra args from the env": `it("keeps quoted extra args from the env together", …)` that sets e.g. `process.env[CLAUDE_ARGS_ENV] = `--append-system-prompt "two words" --x 'a b' c\\ d``, runs the provider, and expects the recorded argv tail to be `["--append-system-prompt", "two words", "--x", "a b", "c d"]` (for codex, followed by `"-"`). This proves the real argv reaching the CLI is right. In `claude.test.ts`, inside the existing `describe("getProvider", …)` block (line 139; the fake `claude` is already on the PATH via `beforeEach`), add `it("fails fast on an unterminated quote in the extra args")`: set `process.env[CLAUDE_ARGS_ENV] = `--x "oops``, then `await expect(getProvider("claude", worktree)).rejects.toThrow("GRAPH_EXECUTION_CLAUDE_ARGS: unterminated double quote")` (the `afterEach` restores the env var).
- **PATTERN**: `src/providers/claude.test.ts:97–102` (argv) and `src/providers/claude.test.ts:139–147` (`getProvider` startup checks).
- **GOTCHA**: the existing "appends extra args" tests with double spaces (`" --max-turns  5 "`) must still pass unchanged.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/providers`

### UPDATE `README.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in "## Requirements", after the line-16 bullet, add a bullet: "- Extra flags for the provider CLI go in `GRAPH_EXECUTION_CLAUDE_ARGS`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_CODEX_ARGS`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_OPENCODE_ARGS` or `GRAPH_EXECUTION_QWEN_ARGS`. They are split like a shell does: `\"two words\"`, `'two words'` and `two\ words` stay one argument; nothing is expanded. An unterminated quote stops the run at startup." (write the real quotes in Markdown, not escaped).
- **GOTCHA**: `src/readme/readme.test.ts` renders the README; run it to make sure nothing breaks.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/readme`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `splitArgs` exists in `src/providers/args.ts` and is the only arg splitter; `grep -rn "split(/\\s+/)" src/providers` finds no `_ARGS_ENV` use.
- [ ] With `GRAPH_EXECUTION_CLAUDE_ARGS='--append-system-prompt "two words"'`, the `claude` CLI receives `--append-system-prompt` and `two words` as two argv entries; same behaviour for codex, opencode and qwen.
- [ ] `"two words"`, `'two words'` and `a\ b` each stay a single argument; unquoted input splits on runs of whitespace exactly as before.
- [ ] An unterminated single/double quote or a trailing backslash throws `Error("<ENV_NAME>: <problem>")`, and `getProvider` rejects with it at startup.
- [ ] No new dependency in `package.json`.
- [ ] README documents the 4 env vars and the quoting rules.
- [ ] `npx vitest run src/providers src/readme` passes.

## Validation commands

```bash
# Type / lint
npx tsc --noEmit
npx eslint .

# Tests for this slice
npx vitest run src/providers src/readme
```
